activities.question: Explain the main idea of Chapter 2.
activities.instructions: Use the source-based options to complete this activity.
activities.sourceTextSummary: Generated from Economics - Introductory Microeconomics, Chapter Chapter 2.

correctItems.text: The consumer has to decide how to spend her income on different goods1.
Most naturally, any consumer will want to get a combination of goods that gives her maximum satisfaction.
This depends on the likes of the consumer and what the consumer can afford to buy.
The 'likes' of the consumer are also called 'preferences'.

More of commodity x provides more satisfaction to the consumer.
Therefore, TUn refers to total utility derived from consuming n units of a commodity x.
Marginal Utility: Marginal utility (MU) is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity.
